name: Music Visualizer Lab
tagline: Turns an audio file into an animated visualizer video for social posts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Audio visualizers are one of the oldest solved problems in computing: FFT the audio, draw bars or a waveform, render frames. A coding agent can wire Web Audio API plus canvas in an afternoon and get a live preview that looks respectable. The only real work is offline rendering, and ffmpeg.wasm or a local ffmpeg call handles that if you accept slow exports. What you will not match quickly is the library of pre-tuned templates and the fact that someone else's GPU does the encoding.
coreLoopDIY: Load a local audio file, render a configurable FFT visualization on canvas over an optional background image, then export frames plus the audio into an MP4.
whatYouLose: A gallery of designer-made templates that already look good without fiddling
Fast server-side rendering instead of your laptop grinding through frames
Reliable export presets for each social platform's aspect ratio and codec quirks
Waveform styles and particle effects you would otherwise have to design yourself
moatNotes: The templates are the product. The math is free.
whyPeopleStillPay: Musicians releasing a single do not want to spend an evening tuning smoothing constants and bar gradients, they want a square video for Instagram by tonight. A hosted tool renders on hardware that is not their laptop and ships presets that already look professional. That convenience is the whole purchase, and it is a real one, just not a technical moat.
notes: The DIY version will look like a 2004 Winamp skin until you spend real time on the aesthetics.
prompt:
Build a local-only music visualizer and video exporter. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack: Vite + vanilla TypeScript + HTML canvas. Web Audio API for analysis. Local ffmpeg binary via a tiny Node script for export. No frameworks, no UI libraries beyond plain CSS.

In scope:
- Drag and drop an audio file (mp3, wav, m4a) from disk. Nothing uploads anywhere.
- Decode it with AudioContext.decodeAudioData and run an AnalyserNode for live preview playback.
- Three visualization modes, selectable: frequency bars, circular spectrum, and mirrored waveform.
- Controls: bar count, smoothing, color gradient (two color pickers), background color, optional background image, and a text overlay for track title and artist.
- Canvas resolution presets: 1080x1080, 1080x1920, 1920x1080.
- Live preview with play/pause and a seek bar.
- Export: render offline, not in realtime. Walk the decoded PCM data in fixed timesteps at 30fps, compute an FFT per frame yourself (implement a small radix-2 FFT, do not rely on AnalyserNode for export since it is realtime-only), draw each frame to an OffscreenCanvas, and write PNGs to ./out/frames.
- A Node script scripts/encode.ts that shells out to ffmpeg to combine ./out/frames/*.png with the original audio into ./out/video.mp4 (h264, yuv420p, faststart).
- Show export progress as a percentage. Warn that a 3 minute track means roughly 5400 frames and will take a while.
- Persist the last-used settings in localStorage.

Out of scope: user accounts, hosted rendering, lyric sync, Spotify or SoundCloud integration, mobile layout, any template gallery.

Deliverables: working dev server via npm run dev, npm run encode for the ffmpeg step, and a README that states ffmpeg must be on PATH. Put nothing in .env since there are no secrets. Keep the whole thing under 600 lines.
